To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the language arts teacher who is able to demonstrate an understanding of the general principles and ideas of the language arts is more successful in helping his or her students to develop their potential for language aptitude than is the teacher who is not as successful in demonstrating an understanding of the language arts.

(a) teacher approach and methodology do not affect student achievement, (b) teacher approach and method do affect the development of student aptitude for language, (c) student achievement in language arts is not a good indicator of student potential for language aptitude.

(1) teacher methodology in the language arts has no significant impact on student achievement, and (2) teacher methodology in language aptitude has a significant impact on student performance on a language aptitude test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between teacher methodology, student aptitude, and achievement.
teacher methodology as an independent variable, and its effect on student performance as the dependent variable.
the relationship between teacher approach to the subject matter and the performance of students on standardized tests of aptitude.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the teacher's approach to language arts instruction does not appear to have a significant effect on student performance.
teacher approach to material in the classroom is a factor which may be considered when evaluating student performance on standardized tests of aptitude and achievement.
the methodology of language arts instruction does not appear to affect student achievement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more the teacher is able to relate the material to the students' own experience, and the less emphasis he places upon specific skills, the greater the student's aptitude for language arts.

the teacher's ability to communicate with students and his or her application of general principles are more important than the teacher's specific knowledge of the subject matter or his or her use of specific teaching techniques.
, while teacher methodology does not appear to affect the achievement of students, it does appear to affect the development of language skills in the students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers who emphasize general principles and ideas are likely to produce students who are better prepared for the rigors of college-level work in the language arts.
teachers can be trained in a variety of methods and approaches to teaching, and that students can learn from all of them.
teachers can be trained to use more effective methods in the classroom and that this will result in better outcomes for students.
